To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the binding of RCAI to asialoGM-1 was studied by RET; and (2) the binding constant was found in the order of 10(4) M-1.
the fluorescence resonance energy transfer method was applied to the binding study of the oligosaccaride moiety of asialoGMl to Ricinus communis lectin.
the binding affinity of the galactosyl group of a neutral glycolipid, asialoganglioside GM1, to the lectin RCA1 was determined for the time by fluorescence resonance enegry transfer (RET).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the binding of lectin to the oligosacchride moiety of a glycosphingoside, i.e. asialo GM1.
the application of RET to the determination of the binding affinity between the oligosaccharyl moiety and a lectin.
the application of RET to study the binding affinity between the oligosacacharide and lectin at the lipid bilayer-water interface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of RCAI to asialoGM 1 in DMPC vesicles is not a cooperative process.
the RET method is useful for the determination of binding affinity of lectins to glycoconjugates in the absence of the protein moiety.
the binding affinity of the carbohydrate moiety of a glycolipid towards lectin is determined by the same parameters as those for the binding of a free oligosaccharides to lectins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RET is a very useful technique for the quantitative analysis of the interaction of a lectin with the carbohydrate moiety at the interface.
the binding constant of a glycolipid is determined by the number of the binding sites and the affinity for each site.
the oligosacacharide moiety of the neutral glycosphin-golipid, GM1, is a potent ligand for the galactose-specific RCAI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding affinity of a glycolipid to a lectin can be determined by fluorescence RET.

the binding affinity of a carbohydrate moiety towards a lectin can be determined by fluorescence RET, if the carbohydrate is incorporated into a lipid membrane and the lectin is labelled with a fluorescent dye.
RET is an effective tool to determine binding constants between lectins and oligosaccharides in complex systems, e.g. at the membrane interface.
